The fits are saved in `data/processed/cv_fits/`. # Cross-validated classifiers ## Design - All training and test clips were pooled and split into 5 folds grouped by recording (all clips of a recording in the same fold) and stratified by species, seed 123 - For each fold, the classifiers were trained on the other 4 folds (early stopping on a random 20% of the training clips) and classified the held-out fold, so every clip has a prediction from a model that never heard its recording - Training and classification used a 400–12,000 Hz bandpass - Hyperparameters were chosen by random search among 30 configurations drawn from the search space of BirdNET-Analyzer's built-in tuner; for each classifier, the simplest configuration within one standard error of the highest out-of-fold macro-averaged AUPRC was selected (rule set before seeing the results, without using the focal bellbird). See the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report - Per-species thresholds maximize F1 on the out-of-fold predictions. A clip is assigned to its highest-confidence species if it reaches that species' threshold, otherwise it is unassigned - The focal bellbird clips are classified by the 5 fold models of the selected configuration: confidences are averaged across models (ensemble) and the out-of-fold thresholds are applied ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} folds <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "folds.csv")) best_cfg <- with(read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "selected_configurations.csv")), setNames(config, model))[models] data.frame(Classifier = model_labels[models], `Selected configuration` = best_cfg, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

consistent. Consistency is the variability within a time window (the recording day): for each clip, the mean cosine similarity of its embedding to each of the other clips of the same type recorded on the same day (day × type combinations with at least 5 clips). Higher values mean more consistent. Unlike the similarity to a centroid of the day's clips (with or without the clip itself), the expected value of this mean pairwise similarity does not depend on the number of clips of the day (only its precision does), which matters because the number of own-song clips per day increased through the season. Two checks: the main model refitted with the (log) number of clips of the day × type combination as a covariate, and a rarefied version in which each day × type combination is repeatedly subsampled to 5 clips (100 draws) and its mean pairwise similarity averaged across draws, modelled at the level of the combination. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} qc <- q_l qc$day_type <- paste(qc$day, qc$species) grp_n <- table(qc$day_type) qc <- qc[qc$day_type %in% names(grp_n)[grp_n >= 5], ] qc$n_group <- as.numeric(grp_n[qc$day_type]) # mean pairwise similarity to the other clips of the group (embeddings are unit length): # (x . sum of the group - x . x) / (n - 1) pairwise_mean <- function(emb, group) { grp_sum <- rowsum(emb, group)[group, , drop = FALSE] (rowSums(emb * grp_sum) - 1) / (as.numeric(table(group)[group]) - 1) } qc$consistency <- pairwise_mean(emb_focal[qc$clip, ], qc$day_type) # rarefied: each group subsampled to 5 clips, mean pairwise similarity averaged over 100 draws rarefy_pairwise <- function(emb, clips, k = 5, n_draw = 100) { mean(replicate(n_draw, { e <- emb[sample(clips, k), ]; sm <- tcrossprod(e); mean(sm[upper.tri(sm)]) })) } set.seed(123) qc_g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(qc, qc$day_type), function(d) data.frame(day = d$day[1], species = d$species[1], julian_day = d$julian_day[1], n_group = nrow(d), consistency = rarefy_pairwise(emb_focal, d$clip), snr = mean(d$snr), snr_long = mean(d$snr_long)))) qc_g$species <- factor(qc_g$species, levels = levels(qc$species)) kable(data.frame(Species = levels(qc$species), Clips = as.numeric(table(qc$species)), `Day × type groups` = tapply(qc$day_type, qc$species, function(x) length(unique(x))), `Mean consistency` = tapply(qc$consistency, qc$species, mean), check.names = FALSE), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Species | Clips| Day × type groups| Mean consistency| |:----------------------|-----:|-----------------:|----------------:| |Keel-billed Toucan | 712| 10| 0.690| |Collared Aracari | 205| 7| 0.653| |Three-wattled Bellbird | 434| 9| 0.613| ::: ```{.r .cell-code} mod12 <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr) + scale(snr_long) + (1 | day/recording), qc, "consistency_pairwise_by_type_through_time") mod12_n <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(log(n_group)) + scale(snr) + scale(snr_long) + (1 | day/recording), qc, "consistency_pairwise_by_type_n_through_time") mod12_r <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr) + scale(snr_long) + (1 | day), qc_g, "consistency_rarefied_by_type_through_time") ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} for (m in list(mod12, mod12_n, mod12_r)) extended_summary(m, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako, remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE) ```

Dialects of the focal bellbird Three-wattled Bellbirds sing in regional dialects. If the focal bellbird produced more than one dialect, and in proportions that changed through time, a day centroid that mixes dialects would make its own song look less consistent, and a shift towards the dialect closer to the reference recordings could look like an improvement. nonlinear change Several trends in the vocal-quality and dialect analyses have intervals that include zero. With only 7–10 recording days per vocalization type in some analyses, such intervals may reflect a lack of precision rather than an absence of change. This section quantifies how large a change the data can rule out, and whether a straight line through time hides a change that is not linear (e.g. an early improvement that then levels off). ## How large a change the data can rule out All measures and dates are standardized, so slopes are in SD of the measure per SD of date. A region of practical equivalence (ROPE) of ± 0.1 SD per SD of date was used, the conventional "negligible" standardized effect (Kruschke 2018). Given the length of the sampling season, this ROPE is equivalent to a change of about ± 0.1 × (season range in SD of date) over the whole season (see the table). Each slope is classified as: - **Change**: the 95% interval excludes zero - **Practically no change**: the 95% interval lies entirely within the ROPE - **Inconclusive**: neither (the data cannot tell a negligible change from a relevant one) The approximate minimum detectable slope is the slope that would be detected (95% interval excluding zero) with 80% probability given the posterior uncertainty: (1.96 + 0.84) × posterior SD of the slope. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rope <- 0.1 type_draws <- function(fit) { post <- as_draws_df(fit) base <- post$b_scalejulian_day
